Ephesians 1:4-5: chosen in him before the foundation of the world and predestinated unto the adoption of children. We did nothing magnanimous; he chose us to wake up in these last days.

note.label: America: Hammer of the Earth

They tried when they murdered Nat Turner and the other men who knew they were Israelites, and through whispers and hushes the word kept going. “For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.” Sometimes our carnal mind says, if we organize we can overthrow the system. No. The governments of this earth are set up by Satan and God allows it; the Most High “setteth up over it the basest of men.” Only God can bring that pyramid down. We get out by “the foolishness of preaching”.

Nahum shows what we wrestle: “Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and robbery; the prey departeth not”. America is the bloody city. She spilled the blood of the tribes of Gad, Reuben and Issachar to steal this country, and on the blood of our brothers and sisters she set up churches, courthouses and school institutions to indoctrinate us. This country is full of lies and robbery.

America is the well-favoured harlot: everybody wants to live in America, and some kissed the ground when they got here and never saw any golden streets. She is the mistress of witchcrafts, and that is the gates of hell. “that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts”: the nations she sold were the two kingdoms of Judah and Ephraim. That is the spiritual wickedness in high places, and it shall not prevail.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh”. These are the same scriptures Esau uses to justify slavery, and that dumb black people use to reject the Bible. But it is not talking about chattel slavery. It is what was read in Leviticus 25 and Exodus: Israel, in a time of stability, still following the laws on selling yourself to work if you were poor or owed debts.

Leviticus says it: “And if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant: But as an hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile”. Then he departs, he and his children, back to his own family, because “Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour”. Rigour is chattel slavery, and God forbade it over a brother.

Colossians says the same: “Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God”. The servants were Israelites, Hebrew servants, hired servants.

Exodus 21 shows the master: “If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.” If his master gave him a wife and she bore children, he could say, “I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free”. Why would he say, I love my master? Because the brother treated him real good. That is what “Servants, obey in all things your masters” is talking about.

precepts.text: Servants, be subject to your masters, not only to the good and gentle.
precepts.point: Onesimus was a servant who fled Philemon, and Paul sent him back as a brother.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.” This is in the slave Bible; Esau used it. But the good and gentle masters and the froward ones were Israelite masters. The law said not to deal with Israel with rigour, meaning hard, yet some of them were like that. The froward ones are the ones who did not really like you.

“For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.”

Why would a master not like his servant? Exodus 22: a thief found breaking in, “If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be blood shed for him; for he should make full restitution; if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.” That is different from a poor brother saying, I lack food, clothing and shelter, will you help me? If I broke into your house, stole all your stuff and got caught, now I have to work for you, and you are not going to like me too much. You have to see him every morning.

So Peter tells servants to be subject even to the froward master, and to take it patiently. It is Israelite servitude under the law, not chattel slavery.

precepts.text: Exhort servants not to purloin but to show all good fidelity.
precepts.point: Onesimus was a servant who fled Philemon, and Paul sent him back as a brother.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again”: not talking back. Esau perverted this. But read on: “Not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.” To purloin is to steal something: sticky fingers, a kleptomaniac. That is what was read in Exodus 22. Paul is dealing with brothers who were stealing, got caught, and were sold to make restitution.

Philemon shows it plainly. Paul met Onesimus while under arrest. He had been a servant to Philemon, and he ran away: “For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever; Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved”. Deal with him like a brother beloved.

Was he a servant because he was poor, or because he did something bad? “If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account”. He owed something because he stole or broke something, and Paul said, put it on my account.

So Paul was dealing with servants who were Hebrews, Israelites in servitude to other Israelites. Chattel slavery came later, when Israel fell by the edge of the sword and was led away captive into all nations, under Rome, Spain and Portugal, France, Britain and the United States.

And dumb black people, seeing how Esau used them, reject the Bible altogether, not knowing it was perverted.

He will bring our seed from the east and gather us from the west, say to the north, give up, and deliver us into the glorious liberty of the children of God. That is the true jubilee.

note.label: Numbers 12: Speaking Against the Man of God

precepts.why:
When Moses cried, “Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee”, the Lord answered, “If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days?” The spit is correction, a father putting his child in her place. Had Miriam been raised to respect the men of the Lord, this would not have befallen her.

“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.” This is a charge to raise children in the fear of the Lord and to teach them to respect the elders and the men of the Lord.

“And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.” Parents who let their children speak evil to the men of the Lord provoke them to wrath and bring judgment on the household, as Miriam was shut out from the camp seven days and the people journeyed not till she was brought in again.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:

“Be strong and of a good courage”, the Lord told Joshua, “for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.” As long as you serve and obey him, there is nothing to be scared of.

precepts.text: Above all taking the shield of faith, and the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God; David went to the battle believing his God would fight for him, carrying the word instead of carnal armor.
precepts.point: Instead of the helmet and the brass, David took his staff, chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, put them in a shepherd's bag, and took his sling in his hand. What he put on instead was the whole armour of God: the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the spirit.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
Saul armed David with his own armor: “he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail.” David girded his sword upon it and assayed to go, “for he had not proved it. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him.”

Instead of the helmet and the brass, David “took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd’s bag”, and “his sling was in his hand”. What he put on instead was the whole armour of God: “Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked. We are fighting against Satan, and Satan has an agenda to destroy the children of Israel; the rest of the people caught up in the system are collateral damage to him.

Book read in class, Trauma Letters, on Erik Erikson's stages of development: human development occurs across eight sequential stages, each presenting a critical psychological challenge. When a child successfully navigates each stage, they build the foundation for the next; when stages are disrupted by absence, neglect, trauma, or instability, the unresolved tension carries forward into every phase of life. The infant who does not develop trust carries a deep seated suspicion of the world; the toddler who is not affirmed grows into an adult plagued by insecurity and self doubt; the adolescent who does not form a stable identity may spend decades searching for themselves in the wrong places: relationships, achievements, or addictions. Is this not our life? And they knew it, and made sure we grew up in these conditions.

Childhood trauma is not merely a past event: when developmental steps are missed, the wound is carried forward, shaping adult thought patterns, relational expectations, and spiritual identity. Healing must address the stage at which the wound occurred, not the surface symptoms. That means you have to go back, find where it took place, and heal from that point: forgive your father, forgive your mother, and let it go.

The book also lays out the divine design of parental guidance: train up a child in the way he should go (Proverbs 22:6); parents are appointed as the primary conduit through which God's wisdom, law, and love flow into the next generation (Deuteronomy 6). When parents are absent, wounded, or disengaged, a door is opened for trauma, confusion, and spiritual vulnerability; we open up portals to Satan.

A curse is a pattern of traumatic, oppressive, destructive conditions that operate generationally: systemic injustice, family dysfunction, cycles of addiction, emotional neglect, mass fatherlessness, poverty, broken covenant.
